text:
alex: Heads-up — prod p99 jumped ~120ms this morning around 07:13 UTC. I grabbed an nsys trace and the timeline shows repeated cudaMalloc spikes during the model warmup phase causing tail latency bumps.

deploy-bot: Deployed inference-runtime @ commit abc1234 (rollout started 1854318000) :rocket:

maria: saw the same in canary last night, good catch. Any relation to the kernel selector changes in that commit?

sam: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? or the nsys flame view timestamps?

alex: here's the relevant excerpt from the nsys timeline (trimmed):

```
Time(ms)  Event
0-10      kernel: fused_attention_v2 (fast path)
10-12     kernel: matmul_q8_optimized
12-18     cudaMalloc(temporary)  <-- small spike
18-22     kernel: fused_attention_v2_workspace_setup
22-26     cudaMalloc(temporary)  <-- repeated
26-34     kernel: fallback_matmul_fp32  <-- larger kernel chosen occasionally
34-40     cudaFree(temporary)
```

alex: Note the pattern: when selector picks fallback_matmul_fp32 we see extra cudaMallocs and fragmentation on the GPU memory arena. The allocs are small (~64-512KB) but very frequent during batch boundary transitions.

jia: interesting. That looks like a workspace allocation pattern. New selector may choose kernels that request dynamic workspace. If our pool allocator returns non-contiguous small chunks we get many cudaMallocs.

maria: also correlate with KV cache activity: when prefix caching gets evicted we re-alloc per-request buffers. I saw bursts of kv_cache_evict events right before the alloc spikes.

sam: can you share the exact nsys command you ran? would like to reproduce locally.

alex: ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,kernels,osrt --sample=none -o /tmp/trace_prod nsys_collect -- ./inference_server --config prod.yml` then opened timeline in Nsight. For a targeted alloc timeline: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,mem --sample=none -o alloc_trace ./inference_server --repro small_batch`

maria: also helpful: run perfetto with the GPU heap walker so we can see arena fragmentation over time. Command we use: `python tools/trace_perfetto.py --pid $PID --out /tmp/trace.pb` then load in UI.

jia: quick hypothesis: the kernel selector change added one more candidate kernel (fallback fp32) that requests workspace via the runtime API instead of preallocating from our arena pool. That triggers cudaMalloc instead of pool_alloc and defeats reuse.

sam: if true, two mitigations: 1) change selector to prefer kernels that use our pool (heuristic by workspace allocation flag), 2) make the pool intercept cudaMalloc calls during warmup and convert them to arena allocations (fast fix).

alex: I prototyped a runtime patch locally: force selector to prefer quantized kernels for sequence length <= 128 and preallocate workspaces. p99 dropped by ~80ms in the local replay.

maria: nice. We should also add metrics: `gpu.cudamalloc.count` and `gpu.pool.alloc_miss` with tags for model+kernel so we can alert on regressions.

sam: +1. Also add an annotation in the rollout that indicates the selector change so we can roll back quickly.

jia: on fragmentation: try increasing the arena slab size from 4MB to 16MB for the KV cache arena. In my experiments that cut small allocations by ~70% because we reuse larger contiguous slabs.

alex: did a short A/B: arena=4MB => 120 alloc spikes/min, arena=16MB => 35 alloc spikes/min on same replay. I'll push the change to a canary.

maria: action items: @maria will add the two metrics and a Grafana panel; @sam will add selector telemetry to indicate kernel workspace type; @alex will push the arena bump to canary and attach fresh nsys trace.

sam: also tagging perfbot to run nightly bake with the new selector: `perfbot run nightly --suite=v2-selector`

perfbot: scheduled nightly job `v2-selector` (ETA 12:30 UTC)

alex: thanks. If the canary looks good we'll rollback the kernel selector change if needed and land the arena bump.

maria: FYI I'll prepare a short perf note for the release docs mentioning this regression and mitigation steps.

alex: uploading the full alloc_trace to /artifacts/1854321987/alloc_trace.nsys for anyone who wants to dig in.

sam: perfect. ping me once canary is up and I'll grab a perfetto heap trace.

alex: will do. :thumbsup:
